title: Table rows with h="0" overlap each other; table is missing from PDF export
author: rclinux
body:
**Version:** deckcraft 0.3.0, Linux x86_64 release tarball (Arch-based distro, Wayland)

### What happens
A table on a slide renders with all of its rows drawn on top of each other at the same position. In my test, "1 alpha" and "2 beta" overlap into one unreadable line and the header row ("Col A / Col B") can't be seen. In `deckcraft-cli convert deck.pptx out.pdf` the table text is missing from the PDF entirely (`pdftotext` finds no table text).

Saving back to .pptx keeps the table: LibreOffice opens DeckCraft's re-saved file and shows the table correctly. So the problem looks like it's in layout and rendering, not in loading or saving.

### Probable cause
The table rows have a height of zero:

```xml
<a:tbl> ... <a:tr h="0"> ... </a:tr> <a:tr h="0"> ... </a:tr> <a:tr h="0"> ... </a:tr>
```

In PowerPoint, `a:tr/@h` is a minimum: each row grows to fit its text. DeckCraft appears to use it as an exact height, so every row is placed at y = 0 inside the table frame. pandoc writes `h="0"` for every table, and other generators (python-pptx, scripts) often do too.

### Steps to reproduce
```sh
printf '# Slide\n\n| Col A | Col B |\n|------:|-------|\n| 1 | alpha |\n| 2 | beta |\n' > t.md
pandoc t.md -t pptx -o t.pptx      # pandoc 3.10.2
deckcraft-cli render t.pptx out.png
deckcraft-cli convert t.pptx out.pdf
```

### Expected
Each row is at least tall enough for its text and rows stack vertically, as in PowerPoint and LibreOffice Impress.

title: Linux source build fails: alsa-lib-devel (libasound2-dev) needed but not documented
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Building DeckCraft from source on Linux fails unless the ALSA development headers are installed, and the README doesn't list this requirement.

**Environment:** Fedora 44 (Nobara), x86_64, rustc 1.98.1; deckcraft `main` @ baff6a2

**Steps:**
```sh
git clone https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft && cd deckcraft
cargo build --release -p deckcraft
```

**Result:**
```
error: failed to run custom build command for `alsa-sys v0.3.1`
```
`alsa-sys` comes in through `cpal = "0.16"` in `apps/deckcraft/Cargo.toml`. It needs `alsa.pc`, which pkg-config can't find without the -devel package.

**Fix:** `sudo dnf install alsa-lib-devel` (Debian/Ubuntu: `libasound2-dev`), then the build succeeds.

**Suggestion:** add a short "Building on Linux" note to the README's Quick start listing `alsa-lib-devel` / `libasound2-dev`. WordCraft, GridCraft and PdfCraft built on the same machine without it, so this is only needed for DeckCraft.

title: Linux (GNOME Wayland): window title bar doesn't match the desktop theme
author: fqazzazee
body:
## Environment

- Fedora 44, GNOME Shell 50.5, Wayland session, 167% display scaling
- Built from source at `4b09f35`

## Title bar doesn't follow the GNOME theme (Wayland)

On GNOME Wayland, the app draws its own title bar. This app shows winit's plain fallback bar, which
ignores the GNOME theme, dark mode and button layout.

The workspace sets `eframe = { version = "0.36", default-features = false }` (`Cargo.toml:66`),
which also drops winit's default `wayland-csd-adwaita` feature, so `sctk-adwaita` isn't in
`Cargo.lock`.

Possible fixes:

- Enable `winit/wayland-csd-adwaita`, so the title bar follows GNOME's look and light/dark mode, or
- Draw an in-app title bar, as PhotoCraft does on Linux.

Workaround: start the app through Xwayland (`env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY deckcraft`), so GNOME draws a real
title bar.

Same issue in GridCraft, with more detail: https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/54

title: Animated GIFs show only their first frame (no playback, no pause)
author: DimaSmaha
body:
## Problem

  An animated GIF inserted into a presentation, or imported with a PPTX, stays frozen on its first frame. It doesn't play in the editor or in the slide show, and there's no way to play or pause it.

  ## Steps to reproduce

  1. Run `cargo run --release -p deckcraft`.
  2. Insert an animated GIF (Insert ▸ Picture), or open a PPTX that contains one.
  3. Look at it in the editor, then start the slide show.

  **Expected:** the GIF plays (loops) in the editor and in the show, and you can pause and resume it, like PowerPoint's corner play/pause button.

  **Actual:** only the first frame is shown, in both views.

  ## Cause

  `crates/render/src/images.rs` decodes every picture with `image::load_from_memory(..).to_rgba8()`, which keeps only the first frame. The editor and the show then cache the rendered slide, and
  nothing redraws it over time.

  ## Proposed fix

  - Decode all GIF frames and draw the frame for each GIF's play time (exports keep the first frame).
  - Redraw only when a GIF reaches its next frame.
  - Add a play/pause button on hover, plus a `media.gifPlay` command so the CLI, control channel and MCP can do the same.

  ## Environment

  - Windows 11
  - DeckCraft 0.3.0 (`main` at 4b09f35)

title: Add a System theme option that follows the macOS light/dark appearance

body:
## Summary

Add a System choice to DeckCraft's interface theme setting that follows the macOS light/dark appearance live, so the app changes with the rest of the desktop when macOS switches appearance automatically.

## Problem to solve

macOS can switch between Light and Dark appearance automatically (System Settings → Appearance → Auto changes it at sunset and sunrise), and many Mac apps offer a "System" theme choice that tracks it.

DeckCraft offers only a manual light/dark switch. `Brightness` in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` has only `Light` (the default) and `Dark`, persisted as `brightness` in `ui.json`. title: Text in flipped shapes is drawn mirrored
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Text in a flipped shape is drawn mirrored. `flipH` mirrors the glyphs left to right, and `flipV` mirrors them upside down. A common case: the label on a "left arrow" made by flipping a right arrow reads backwards.

**Repro:** a slide with a `rightArrow` shape that has `<a:xfrm flipH="1">` and the text "Next" (python-pptx: add the shape, then set `flipH="1"` on its `a:xfrm`).

**Expected (PowerPoint):** flips mirror the geometry, never the text. `flipH` text stays upright and readable; `flipV` (or both flips) turns it 180°. The same applies inside flipped groups.

**Actual:** mirrored glyphs. Clicking the label also places the caret at the mirrored position, so a double-click selects the wrong characters.

**Cause:** `shape()` in `crates/render/src/lib.rs` draws text with the shape's full transform, flip scale included. The editing caret and hit-testing use the same transform.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, deckcraft `main` @ 4b09f35 (0.3.0).

Fix in #35.

title: Date fields are blank, or show another slide's fixed date text
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Automatic date fields (`<a:fld type="datetime1">`, `datetimeFigureOut`, …) show the deck-wide fixed date text instead of the date. On most decks they are blank. If any one slide has fixed date text in its date placeholder, every slide's date field shows that text.

**Repro:** a 4-slide deck whose footers use `datetime1`, `datetimeFigureOut`, a fixed text "Fixed date text" (plain text in that slide's date placeholder) and `datetime4`.

**Expected (PowerPoint):** the automatic fields show today's date in their type's format (e.g. 10/9/2026, October 9, 2026). The slide with fixed text shows its text.

**Actual:** all four slides show "Fixed date text". Without that slide, all four would be blank.

**Cause:** `SlideFields::field` (`crates/render/src/lib.rs`) returns `header_footer.date_text` for every `datetime*` field. The reader (`header_footer()` in `crates/pptx/src/read/mod.rs`) fills that from the first slide whose date placeholder has plain text.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, deckcraft `main` @ 4b09f35 (0.3.0).

Fix in #36.

author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Give desktop installations of DeckCraft a documented CLI invocation that people, scripts, and agents can use on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

## Problem to solve

Including a CLI executable in a package does not always make a shell command available. Windows installs the CLI beside the app; Linux native packages install it in `/usr/bin`, while AppImage and Flatpak keep it inside their package. macOS publishes a separate CLI download. Users need a supported invocation that matches their desktop installation without guessing its location or modifying global settings.

title: Feature request: AutoSave & version history to storage you own (local/NAS, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3/R2 via rclone), slide-level sharing, and no silent data loss on .pptx
author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR
PowerPoint's AutoSave, version history and co-authoring depend on OneDrive/SharePoint. Please add an open equivalent: a central "Save target" so a deck can autosave and keep versions on storage the user owns, with slide-level sharing later. Opt-in, no vendor server, no telemetry.

## Why (and why now)
- The README says unsaved work is kept by AutoRecover, which is a good base. This issue extends it to remote targets and versions.
- Related data-loss reports: #60 (Close silently discards an edited presentation), #105 (saving defaults to the *.deckcraft extension), and the PPTX round-trip losses in #70, #72, #74, #77 (comments, replies, audio/video options, animation rewind). A cloud autosave that silently replaces a .pptx with a lossy re-export would make these worse, so the proposal below is built around not doing that.

## How PowerPoint does it
- Microsoft documents co-authoring for PowerPoint, Word and OneNote on OneDrive and SharePoint. File > Save pushes your changes, pulls others' changes and updates version history on the server.
- AutoSave applies only to files on OneDrive/SharePoint; the first edit creates a version, then roughly one every 10 minutes. Otherwise only AutoRecover.
- The server merges; clients only negotiate locks and show a merge prompt when automatic merge fails.

## What DeckCraft has today (README only)
Native `.deckcraft`, .pptx open/save, AutoRecover, comments, sections, notes, embedded audio/video, 200+ commands (CLI/control channel/MCP), web build.

## Proposal
**Phase 0:** make AutoRecover a real write-ahead journal (atomic writes, recovery prompt, `file.autoSave` command). Fix the "close without asking" path (#60) first; it outranks this feature.
**Phase 1, Save target** (shared building blocks below). **Autosave writes the lossless native `.deckcraft` working copy to the target;** `.pptx` is written on explicit Save/Export, or via an opt-in "keep .pptx in sync" that warns about known lossy features. Keep the original .pptx …

title: Window decorations and title bar inconsistent with VectorCraft / PhotoCraft
author: dylanmtaylor

### Description
The window decorations and title bar handling in `deckcraft` are inconsistent with the standard established in VectorCraft (PR #969) and PhotoCraft (PR #1903).

### Current Behavior
- On Windows and Linux, the application either does not draw client-side decorations/caption buttons or lacks consistent custom title bar handling.
- There is no option for users to toggle `System Title Bar` (native OS window decorations) in Preferences/User Interface.

### Desired Behavior
Standardize title bar and window decoration architecture to match VectorCraft:
1. Support custom client-side titlebar and window caption buttons (Minimize, Maximize/Restore, Close) with edge resize zones.
2. Provide a `System Title Bar` preference under User Interface to allow users to switch back to native OS decorations on Windows/Linux if desired.

author: gNovp
body:

This can today be easily done with copy/pasting, but the copies are then unlinked (which makes it challenging when that specific content needs to be updated quickly before a presentation). Of course, the Slide Master solves a part of this issue, but it's far from ideal.

What if we had a new entry in the rightclick menu: Paste as Reference.
This button would link the elements together, meaning that an edit on any of these would instantly reflect on all the instanced copies.

This could apply to any element: text fields, images/icons, shapes, media, and could be a huge time saver (especially in huge presentations).
Of course, this feature could be specific to the .deckcraft file format (and copies unlinked if saving as .pptx, as it could be tricky to implement here, even if technically speaking, media in current PPTX files are already instances from ppt/media folder)

author: gNovp
body:

It could be great to add a new side panel to DeckCraft, listing all the already imported objects (video, images, sounds, icons...) into the current slide deck, ideally presented via thumbnails. Then when clicking on one object of that list, having the option to just add it to the current slide, or add a reference to that object (allowing edits like in #122 ) would be a great time saver.

author: gNovp
body:

Building on the Library feature from #123 , it could be great to add to the context menu of selected objects (groups, or single elements like text fields, media etc) a "Favorite" entry. Of course, Morph transitions can be used to workaround this issue (duplicating the slide, and repositionning the object). But in lots of cases it could be great to just be able to scroll an element (text, image, or even group) in place.

A list control could be added in the "Shape Format" tab, right under the size controls (Height and Width), with 4 choices:

- Scroll horizontally
- Scroll vertically
- Scroll horizontally and vertically

body:

When the video recording feature will be worked on for DeckCraft, it could be great to ask first to the user the mode of recording:
- Capture and embed (the current mode in Powerpoint, integrating the webcam video as an object in each slide)
- Capture for editing

The latter mode would still record the webcam, audio and timings, but it could place the files after the recording in the same folder as the presentation file itself. Thus, after the recording session, the user would then get: the presentation .deckcraft or .pptx file, a _webcam.mp4_ file and a _slideshow.mp4_ file.

And as a bonus, a precut FilmCraft project file embedding these files could also be placed here (or more generally a XML or CSV editlist that could be imported into any Video editing app). This would help tie in the apps in the Craft open ecosystem.

But on more complex presentations (with lots of references to external sources, or links to other slides etc), it can be difficult to work with that, as there is no place showing all links on a given slide.

It could be great to add a new Panel to DeckCraft (similar to the Animation pane, or Selection pane etc): the Action pane.
Displayed on the side of the current slide, it would allow to review all interactive elements in the current slide, set up if they would be triggered by click, keypress, or timer, etc...The pane could be divided into 3 parts:

- Actions on slide arrival
_Triggered when entering the current slide_

- Actions during the slide is displayed
_This section would show all objects having hyperlinks to external elements (URLs, files, etc), and links to other slides_

- Actions when leaving the slide
_Triggered when the current slide is left for an other one_

title: [Bug] macOS: double-clicking a .pptx in Finder shows "DeckCraft cannot open files in the Office Open XML presentation format"
author: SommerEngineering
body:
I made DeckCraft the default app for `.pptx` files on macOS. Double-clicking a `.pptx` in Finder
launches DeckCraft, but instead of the presentation, macOS shows this alert:

> The document “NAME.pptx” could not be opened. DeckCraft cannot open files in the “Office Open XML presentation” format.

Dragging the same file into the DeckCraft window opens it without problems, so the file itself is fine.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make DeckCraft the default app for `.pptx` files in Finder.
2. Double-click a `.pptx` file in Finder.

### Expected

DeckCraft opens the presentation.

### Actual

DeckCraft starts and shows the alert above. No presentation opens.

### Likely cause

The `Info.plist` of the v0.5.0 bundle has no `CFBundleDocumentTypes`, and winit 0.30 doesn't handle
the `kAEOpenDocuments` Apple event that Finder sends. AppKit then handles the event itself, finds no
document class for the type, and shows the alert. Drag & drop goes through winit, which is why it works.

#68 looks like it fixes exactly this: it adds the document types and a `kAEOpenDocuments` handler.

### Environment

- DeckCraft 0.5.0 (build a98df49b)
- macOS 27.0.1, Apple silicon

title: Arabic Language Support and Comprehensive Right-to-Left (RTL) Presentation Workflows
author: Wyetgf
body:
### Overview

If DeckCraft aims to become a complete open-source replacement for Microsoft PowerPoint, Arabic support should be treated as a first-class architectural and usability requirement—not merely as a translation of menus or the ability to display Arabic characters.

A reliable Arabic presentation workflow requires coordinated support across the user interface, text layout engine, slide model, editing tools, visual objects, charts, tables, animations, notes, import/export, accessibility, and automated testing.

The goal is not only to make Arabic text appear correctly. The application should ensure that Arabic and mixed Arabic–Latin content can be created, edited, formatted, presented, imported, exported, and reopened without unexpected changes in direction, ordering, alignment, positioning, or interaction behavior.

This request intentionally separates the requirements into specific functional areas. These are not repetitions of the same requirement: correct RTL interface mirroring, bidirectional text layout, cursor movement, chart labels, object positioning, animation direction, and file round-tripping are separate technical problems that can fail independently.

### 1. Fully mirrored RTL user interface

When Arabic is selected as the application language, DeckCraft should provide a complete RTL interface.

This should include:

- Mirroring of the main application layout, including sidebars, slide thumbnails, inspectors, navigation panels, dialogs, menus, and contextual menus.

- Correct ordering and alignment of buttons, tabs, breadcrumbs, dropdowns, toggles, checkboxes, radio buttons, and segmented controls.
- RTL-aware slide navigation and thumbnail presentation.
- Proper alignment of icons and labels without incorrectly mirroring icons whose meaning is not directional.

title: Chart render: automatic title (autoTitleDeleted=0, single series) is not drawn
author: rex4539
body:
## Summary

`deckcraft-cli render` draws no title on a single-series chart that has `<c:autoTitleDeleted val="0"/>` and no explicit `<c:title>`. PowerPoint and LibreOffice both show an automatic title made from the series name (`Sales`). Charts made by python-pptx and other generators often rely on this auto title, so in deckcraft they silently lose their heading.

**Actual (deckcraft):** no title above the plot area.
**Expected (PowerPoint, LibreOffice):** the bold title `Sales` centred above the plot.

## Steps to reproduce

A single-series clustered column chart made with python-pptx 1.0.2 (`uv run --with python-pptx make.py`):

```python
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
from pptx.util import Inches

prs = Presentation()
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
data = CategoryChartData()
data.categories = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma"]
data.add_series("Sales", (42.1, 18.7, 6.3))
slide.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED, Inches(1), Inches(1), Inches(8), Inches(5.5), data)
prs.save("chart-single-series.pptx")
```

```
deckcraft-cli render chart-single-series.pptx --all out/
```

Reference: the same file exported to PDF by Microsoft PowerPoint for Mac (via AppleScript `save … as save as PDF`).

The chart XML has `<c:autoTitleDeleted val="0"/>`, no `<c:title>`, no `<c:varyColors>` element, and no `<c:max>`/`<c:majorUnit>` on the value axis.

## Environment

- deckcraft-cli 0.5.0 (also seen on 0.4.0), `deckcraft-cli-0.5.0-macos-universal.zip` from the release
- macOS 15.8.2, Intel x86_64
- Reference renderer: Microsoft PowerPoint for Mac. LibreOffice 26.8 matches PowerPoint on the title and the axis.

title: 0.5.0: `render --help` writes a PNG named `--help` instead of printing help (unknown --flags become the output path)
author: charles-hood
body:
**Environment:** deckcraft-cli 0.5.0, macOS universal zip (`deckcraft-cli-0.5.0-macos-universal.zip`), macOS on Apple silicon. The parser is unchanged at `main` (be14248), see below.

## What happens

`deckcraft-cli render --help` does not print help. It exits 0 and writes a 1920x1080 PNG named `--help` into the current directory:

```
$ deckcraft-cli render --help
--help (1920×1080)
$ echo $?
0
$ ls -la -- --help
-rw-r--r--  1 charles  wheel  42778 Oct 11 14:13 --help
$ file -- --help
--help: PNG image data, 1920 x 1080, 8-bit/color RGBA, non-interlaced
```

The image is slide 1 of a blank new document (no input file and no `--sample`, so `open()` falls through to `file.new`).

The other subcommands do not render anything, but none of them treats `--help` as a request for help either:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `render --help` | writes `./--help` (PNG), exit 0 |
| `render -h` | `render needs an output path`, exit 1 |
| `info --help` | `--help: not a presentation DeckCraft can read` |
| `convert --help` | `convert needs IN and OUT` |
| `run --help` | `unknown option \`--help\`` (the right behaviour, just no help text) |
| `commands --help` | `[]` (filters the registry by the string "--help") |
| `deckcraft-cli --help` (top level) | prints the usage block, exit 1 |

## Cause

In `apps/deckcraft-cli/src/main.rs`, `render()` matches its arguments with a positional-input guard and then a catch-all:

```rust

    if input.is_none()
        && !sample
        && !other.starts_with("--")
        && out.is_none()
        && !(other.ends_with(".png") || other.ends_with(".jpg"))
        || (input.is_none() && !sample && std::path::Path::new(other).is_file()) =>
{
    input = Some(other.to_string())
}
other => out = Some(other.to_string()),
```

Any token starting with `--` that is not one of `--sample`, `--slide`, `--all`, `--edit`, `--scale` skips the input arm (because of `!other.starts_with("--")`) and lands in the catch-all, which makes it the output path. So …

title: Export the deck as an animated GIF (File ▸ Export ▸ Create an Animated GIF)
author: Mathiasko
body:
## Problem

There is no way to turn a presentation into an animated GIF. `docs/file-format-parity.md` lists "Animated GIF of the deck" as export: no, and `docs/gaps.md` has it under "No video or animated GIF export" (checklist row P2, `docs/parity-checklist.md`). PowerPoint's File ▸ Export ▸ Create an Animated GIF is a common way to share a short deck or a single animated slide.

## Expected

File ▸ Export ▸ Animated GIF (and `deckcraft-cli`, `file.export`, MCP) writes a looping GIF of the deck, with options like PowerPoint's:

- size (e.g. Medium, Large, or a pixel width),
- how long each slide shows, in seconds (default 5),
- loop forever or play once,
- which slides (all, or a range).

## Proposed first version

- One frame per slide at the chosen delay, rendered with the existing slide renderer.
- Encode with the `image` crate's GIF encoder (already a dependency), with a per-frame palette.
- A `file.export` format `gif` with `{width?, secondsPerSlide?, loop?, slides?}` params, an Export menu entry, and the same through the CLI and MCP export tool.
- Skip hidden slides.

Out of scope for the first version (and tracked under video export): animating transitions and build animations between frames.

## Tests

- Export a generated 3-slide deck; decode the GIF and check the frame count, size, per-frame delay and loop flag.
- Params are validated (width and delay bounds, slide range), with no panics on hostile values.

Related: #39 (GIF playback inside slides), the MP4/MOV video export gap in `docs/file-format-parity.md`.

I would like to suggest adding OSC (Open Sound Control) support to DeckCraft. Incorporating OSC would make presentation navigation and integration with live production setups much more reliable, lightweight, and versatile compared to current mobile/remote and external solutions in other software.

title: Saving as .potx or .ppsx writes a regular presentation (wrong main content type)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Saving with a `.potx` or `.ppsx` name writes an ordinary presentation. The Save dialog has no type filter, so you pick the format by typing the extension. `[Content_Types].xml` declares the main part as `presentationml.presentation.main+xml` for all three extensions, and the `.pptx`, `.potx` and `.ppsx` outputs are byte-identical. A template should use `presentationml.template.main+xml` and a slideshow `presentationml.slideshow.main+xml`. Other apps go by the content type, so the file opens as a normal deck: not as a new untitled copy for a template, and not straight into Slide Show for a slideshow. I haven't been able to check how PowerPoint treats the mismatch.

**Repro:**
```sh
deckcraft-cli run --sample --save deck.deckcraft
for e in pptx potx ppsx; do deckcraft-cli convert deck.deckcraft deck.$e; done
cmp deck.pptx deck.potx && cmp deck.pptx deck.ppsx && echo identical
unzip -p deck.potx '\[Content_Types\].xml' | grep -o 'presentationml\.[a-z]*\.main+xml'
```
The same happens with File ▸ Save As… and a `.potx` / `.ppsx` file name.

**Expected:** `presentationml.template.main+xml` for `.potx`, `presentationml.slideshow.main+xml` for `.ppsx`.

**Actual:** `presentationml.presentation.main+xml` for both; the files are identical to the `.pptx`.

**Cause:** `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs` sends `"pptx" | "potx" | "ppsx"` to the same `deckcraft_pptx::export(doc)`, and `crates/pptx/src/write/mod.rs` only has `CT_PRES`. Reading is fine: a `.potx` or `.ppsx` with the correct content types opens in DeckCraft.

**Environment:** Linux (Fedora 44, KDE Plasma, Wayland), DeckCraft 0.4.0. On `main` @ 0ec0cc5 the only changes since are CI and packaging.

title: Markdown outlines: '#' stays in slide titles and top-level '-' items become slides
author: LloydNicholson
body:
File ▸ Open's **Outline** filter accepts `.txt` and `.md`, and both are read with the plain outline format: each unindented line is a slide title, and tab or 2-space indented lines are bullets. A Markdown outline written the usual way therefore gives a broken deck.

**Repro:** open this `outline.md` (or `deckcraft-cli info outline.md`):
```md
# Intro
- Point one
- Point two
  - Sub point

# Second
- More
```

**Expected:** 2 slides: **Intro** (bullets *Point one*, *Point two*, sub-bullet *Sub point*) and **Second** (*More*).

**Actual:** 5 slides titled `# Intro`, `Point one`, `Point two`, `# Second`, `More`. The `#` stays in the titles, and every top-level list item becomes its own slide.

**Cause:** `open_presentation` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs` treats `.md` exactly like `.txt`. `outline_to_slides` (`crates/format/src/lib.rs`) strips leading `-` / `*` / `•` but not `#`, and decides slide vs bullet by indentation alone.

**Suggestion:** for `.md`, read ATX headings (`#`, `##`, …) as slide titles and the list items under a heading as bullets nested by their list indentation, and keep today's behaviour for `.txt`.

**Environment:** Linux (Fedora 44, KDE Plasma, Wayland), DeckCraft 0.4.0. On `main` @ 0ec0cc5 the only changes since are CI and packaging.

title: Proposal: a Git-friendly folder format for presentations (`.deck/`: one JSON file per slide)
author: pierrevbc
body:
## Problem

A `.deckcraft` file is a zip whose `presentation.json` is one compact line. In Git it is an opaque
binary: no readable diff, no review, and any two branches that touch the same deck conflict on the
whole file. Teams that keep decks next to their code or documents (consulting deliverables, docs
sites, release notes, course material) can't review or merge slide changes, and agents that edit
decks through the CLI or MCP leave changes nobody can read in a pull request.

DeckCraft is well placed to fix this: its model is already a clean, deterministic JSON document, and
`crates/format` already writes a reproducible zip (1980 timestamps, stable entry order).

## Proposal

An alternative on-disk form of the same document, a folder that DeckCraft opens and saves directly:

```text
offer.deck/
├── deck.json            # format + version + the remaining presentation fields
├── slides.order         # slide order and sections, one slide key per line
├── slides/
│   ├── 01JA7Q3M5K8X9Y2Z3A4B5C6D7E.json   # one slide per file
│   └── 01JA7Q4B2DQ7W1N8V3C5X6Z9KM.json
├── masters/
│   ├── 3.json           # one master with its layouts and theme
│   ├── notes.json       # notesMaster, if any
│   └── handout.json     # handoutMaster, if any
├── media-meta/
│   └── 412.json         # {"id":412,"name":"image3.png","contentType":"image/png","sha256":"9f2c…"}
└── media/
    └── 9f2c41….png      # bytes named by SHA-256 (works well with Git LFS, optional)
```

`slides.order`:

```text
# slides.order v1
section: Introduction
01JA7Q3M5K8X9Y2Z3A4B5C6D7E
01JA7Q4B2DQ7W1N8V3C5X6Z9KM
section: Appendix
01JA7R0P6T3S2D9F8G7H6J5K4L
```

Rules:

1. **Lossless.** Loading the folder gives a `Presentation` equal to the one saved. Same model, same
   `load()` + `repair()` path; the folder is just another container next to the zip.
2. **Canonical JSON.** 2-space indentation, LF, final newline, unescaped UTF-8, keys in model order,

title: SmartArt: text upside down on rotated shapes (dsp:txXfrm ignored)
author: alin742
body:
## What happens
In a deck with a SmartArt list whose shapes are rotated 180°, every text in the SmartArt renders upside down. PowerPoint and LibreOffice Impress show it upright.

Seen in DeckCraft 0.6.0 (`0ec0cc5`), both in the app and with `deckcraft-cli render`.

## Cause
The SmartArt drawing part (`ppt/diagrams/drawingN.xml`) stores, per shape, the shape's rotation in `dsp:spPr/a:xfrm` and a separate text rectangle `dsp:txXfrm` with its own rotation that counter-rotates the text:

```xml
<dsp:sp>
  <dsp:spPr><a:xfrm rot="10800000">…</a:xfrm>…</dsp:spPr>
  <dsp:txBody>…<a:t>Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA)</a:t>…</dsp:txBody>
  <dsp:txXfrm rot="10800000"><a:off …/><a:ext …/></dsp:txXfrm>
</dsp:sp>
```

DeckCraft never reads `dsp:txXfrm` (no reference anywhere in `crates/`). `smartart()` in `crates/pptx/src/read/shapes.rs` imports the drawing's shapes through the normal `sp()` path, so the text inherits the shape's 180° rotation and the 180° correction is lost.

## Expected
Text is laid out in the `txXfrm` rectangle with the `txXfrm` rotation applied, which here puts it upright, as in PowerPoint.

## Related
The same root cause rotates the text 90° on shapes with `rot="5400000"` / `txXfrm rot="-5400000"` (separate issue).

title: SmartArt: text rotated 90° and wrapped letter by letter in rotated list boxes
author: alin742
body:
## What happens
In a SmartArt "vertical block list" (a label box on the left, a bullet box on the right), the bullet text in the right-hand boxes renders rotated 90° and wraps after one or two letters per line, e.g.

```
• Is
th
er
e
...
```

PowerPoint and LibreOffice show normal horizontal bullets ("• Is there any concern?").

Seen in DeckCraft 0.6.0 (`0ec0cc5`).

## Cause
Same root cause as #231. The bullet boxes are drawn as shapes rotated 90°, with a `dsp:txXfrm` that rotates the text back by −90° and gives the text its own (wide) rectangle:

```xml
<dsp:spPr><a:xfrm rot="5400000">…</a:xfrm>…</dsp:spPr>
…
<dsp:txXfrm rot="-5400000"><a:off …/><a:ext …/></dsp:txXfrm>
```

Because `dsp:txXfrm` is ignored, the text keeps the shape's 90° rotation and is wrapped to the shape's short side.

## Expected
Text is laid out in the `txXfrm` rectangle with its rotation, i.e. horizontal and full width.

title: Render: line widths scaled by group child-coordinate scale, slide turns black
author: alin742
body:
## What happens
A slide containing a group drawn in a small legacy child coordinate system renders almost entirely black. PowerPoint and LibreOffice render it normally (bell curves, lines, labels).

Seen in DeckCraft 0.6.0 (`0ec0cc5`).

## Cause
The groups use child coordinates in the old master-unit range, so the group-to-child scale is about 1587×:

```xml
<p:grpSpPr><a:xfrm>
  <a:off x="284957" y="2284419"/><a:ext cx="5907087" cy="3032125"/>
  <a:chOff x="1111" y="1899"/><a:chExt cx="3721" cy="1910"/>
</a:xfrm></p:grpSpPr>
```

The children are ordinary lines and freeforms with `<a:ln w="9525">` (0.75 pt) in `tx1` (black).

`stroke()` in `crates/render/src/lib.rs` builds the `kurbo::Stroke` with the line width in points but strokes it under the full transform `m`, which includes the group's child-space scale from `group_child_affine`. The 0.75 pt line therefore becomes ~1190 pt wide, and the black strokes cover the whole slide. Removing the two such groups from the slide makes it render normally; removing any single child does not.

## Expected
As in PowerPoint, a group's child-coordinate scale does not change line widths (only the slide/view scale does). The stroke width should be compensated for the group scale (or the path transformed before stroking).

Probably also worth checking: dash patterns and arrowheads, which derive their size from the line width.

title: Pictures: a:biLevel (black-and-white) recolor effect not supported
author: alin742
body:
## What happens
A logo picture on a slide layout is invisible: the slide shows only an empty cyan background with a faint outline of the letters. PowerPoint shows the logo in white and black.

Seen in DeckCraft 0.6.0 (`0ec0cc5`).

## Cause
The picture is a cyan-on-transparent PNG placed over a full-slide rectangle filled with the same cyan (`2DC6D6`). PowerPoint makes it visible with the black-and-white (bi-level) recolor effect on the blip:

```xml
<p:blipFill>
  <a:blip r:embed="rId2"><a:biLevel thresh="25000"/></a:blip>
  <a:stretch><a:fillRect/></a:stretch>
</p:blipFill>
```

`a:biLevel` (each pixel becomes black or white depending on whether its luminance is below `thresh`, alpha kept) is not parsed: the blip-effect match in `crates/pptx/src/read/dml.rs` handles `alphaModFix`, `lum`, `grayscl`, `duotone`, `clrChange`, … but not `biLevel`. The picture is drawn with its original cyan, so it vanishes into the background.

## Expected
`a:biLevel` is imported and applied when rendering (and round-tripped on save), so the logo renders white/black as in PowerPoint.

title: [Performance] Noticeable delay when advancing slides in presentation mode
author: LeonardNid
body:
**What happens**
In presentation mode, pressing → (or Space/PageDown) to go to the next slide has a clearly noticeable delay before the new slide appears.

title: Chart legend is always drawn at the bottom: c:legendPos (default "r") is ignored by the renderer
author: Mart95Dev
body:
## Summary

Chart legends are always drawn centred along the bottom, whatever `c:legend/c:legendPos` says. The reader keeps the position (`crates/pptx/src/read/chart.rs:99`, defaulting to `"r"` as the spec does), and the writer writes it back, but `crates/render/src/chart.rs` never looks at it ("// Legend at the bottom.", around line 90). `r` is both the OOXML default and what PowerPoint uses for most charts, so legends that sit to the right of the plot in PowerPoint and LibreOffice end up under it in DeckCraft, and the plot shrinks vertically instead of horizontally.

## Reproduction

Apache POI test data `test-data/slideshow/pie-chart.pptx` (https://github.com/apache/poi/blob/trunk/test-data/slideshow/pie-chart.pptx): one pie chart with `<c:legendPos val="r"/>`.

```
deckcraft-cli convert pie-chart.pptx out.pdf
```

- PowerPoint / LibreOffice: legend (1st Qtr … 4th Qtr) stacked vertically on the right of the pie.
- DeckCraft: legend in one row under the pie.

## Expected

Honour `legendPos`:

- `r` / `l`: a vertical stack, centred vertically, with the plot area narrowed.
- `t` / `b`: a horizontal row (today's behaviour is right for `b`).
- `tr`: top-right corner.
- `c:overlay val="1"`: drawn over the plot without shrinking it.
- `c:legend/c:layout/c:manualLayout`, when present: overrides the position.

## Environment

DeckCraft 0.6.1 (`688c7ef`, main), built from source with `cargo build --release` (Rust 1.95.0), macOS on Apple Silicon. Reference rendering: LibreOffice headless.

title: Security: --control server accepts unauthenticated requests
author: mendy-cohen
body:
I was looking through the DeckCraft source (commit 688c7ef) before trying it out and found a security issue with the control server.

`apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs` listens on `127.0.0.1:<port>` when started with `--control <port>` or `DECKCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`, and runs every JSON line it gets with no authentication. That includes `app.open`, `app.save`, `app.export` and input injection, so any local process can drive the app and read or write files through it.

It also keeps reading after a line that isn't valid JSON, instead of closing the connection. So a browser request to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` with a `text/plain` body (no CORS preflight) might get its body line run, after the HTTP header lines fail to parse. Newer Chrome local-network protections may block that, but other browsers may not.

It's opt-in, so this only matters for people who turn it on. But PhotoCraft (`authentication_reply`) and PdfCraft (`random_token` / `constant_time_eq` in `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`) already require a random token and close the connection on a bad first line.

**Suggested fix:** use the same token handshake as PhotoCraft/PdfCraft (a random token written to a file the MCP wrapper reads), and close the connection when the first request is anything other than a valid `auth`.

GridCraft has the same problem (filed there too). I found this by reading the code, not by testing a running build, so let me know if I misread anything.

title: CLI, MCP and control channel answer agents in words
author: hoblin
body:
## Problem to solve

DeckCraft ships a CLI, an MCP server and a control channel so agents can build decks. An agent can only learn what went wrong from the answer it gets back, and today many answers either point the wrong way or say nothing. I drive `deckcraft-cli` from an AI agent, and one three-card slide took the agent about a hundred commands, many of them spent guessing why a call failed or whether it did anything.

What the agent actually got back:

- `--cmd new=file.new={"blank":true}` (it read `ID` in `--cmd ID[=JSON]` as its own label) answered `new: bad JSON: expected ident at line 1 column 2`. That sends it hunting for a mistake in valid JSON.
- `shape.resize` on shapes from four slides in one `run` answered `no such shape`. It doesn't say which shape, or that ids are looked up on the current slide only.
- `shape.insert {"shape": "roundRect", …}` succeeds and draws a plain rectangle, because the key is `preset`. Unknown keys are dropped silently, so the agent believes its call worked.
- `slide.go {"index": 7}` on a one-slide deck goes to the last slide and reports success; `shape.move` with ids `[260, 999]` moves 260 and answers `1`.
- Calls that succeed answer `null` (`format.size`, `design.background`) or bare JSON like `{"at":[0,13],"id":258}`, so the agent can't tell what changed without rendering.

Others have hit the same silent failures: #95, #96, #97.

## Solution

Every answer says, in words, what happened, and every refusal says what was wrong and how the call is written. Nothing else changes: the commands, their parameters and the input syntax stay as they are.

- A command that has no result of its own answers with what it changed: `changed shape 258 on slide index 0`, `changed the background of every slide`, `nothing changed`.
- Parameters a command doesn't take are refused with the ones it does: ``` `shape.insert` was given `shape`, which it doesn't take. `shape.insert` takes {preset: …, rect: [x,y,w,h] pt, text?: string}. ```…

title: Author a real PowerPoint template from commands
author: hoblin
body:
## Problem to solve

Company decks start from a template: a `.potx` with the company's slide master, layouts, text styles and footers. DeckCraft reads such templates and renders them correctly, but it can't make one. An agent building a company template through the CLI could set the theme, put a logo on the master and add layouts, then got stuck:

1. `format.*` on a master placeholder changed only its prompt text, not the text style slides inherit. Nothing said so; the agent found out from a render.
2. A layout couldn't hide the master's graphics: `design.hideBackgroundGraphics` in layout view changed nothing. So a cover or a dark section layout kept the master's logo.
3. A dark layout couldn't turn its text light; it can't override the colour map.

title: No visible text caret: black on dark slides, and none at all in an empty placeholder
author: xc4pr
body:
**DeckCraft 0.6.1** (AppImage, linux x86_64) on Arch Linux, GNOME 51 (Wayland). The code involved is the same on `main` today.

When I click into a text box I often can't see where I am typing. There are two cases.

### 1. On a dark slide the caret is black
1. New presentation, Design ▸ pick the dark theme "Nocturne" (or open any deck with a dark background and light text).
2. Click into the title and type a word.

Expected: a caret I can see, for example in the colour of the text.
Actual: the caret blinks in black on the dark background. Screenshots taken through the control channel show the caret pixels switching between `#121826` (the background) and `#04060A`.

`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` strokes the caret with `t.caret`, and both `Tokens::light()` and `Tokens::dark()` in `theme.rs` set `caret: Color32::BLACK`. That token follows the app theme, but the caret is drawn on the slide.

### 2. An empty placeholder shows no caret at all
1. New presentation (the default white theme is enough).
2. Click "Click to add title".

Expected: the prompt goes away and a caret blinks where the text will start.
Actual: the placeholder gets its selection frame, but "Click to add title" stays and no caret appears, so nothing tells me the box is ready for typing. Typing does work, and the caret shows up after the first character.

The placeholder's `TextBody` has no paragraphs until something is typed, so `cmd::text::layout_for` produces no lines and `TextLayout::caret` returns `None`. An engine test that asks for the caret at `(0, 0)` of a freshly edited title fails for that reason.

I have a fix for both and will open a PR.

**What happens**

Opening a deck that contains charts and saving it back to .pptx removes every part under `ppt/embeddings/` and the chart relationship files that point to them. author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

Independently, recover a document and terminate before its next recovery checkpoint: the only backup has already been removed. This concerns local crash recovery, not the additional remote-versioning feature proposed in #112.

title: [Audit] File saves use a shared predictable .saving path without exclusive creation
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High (conditional filesystem security and data-integrity risk)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:217-221](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L217-L221) builds `format!("{path}.saving")`, calls ordinary `std::fs::write`, then renames it to the destination. Concurrent saves share that path. Existing files are truncated, and ordinary file opening follows a pre-existing symlink.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Concurrent processes saving the same destination can interfere with each other's temporary bytes or rename. If an untrusted party can create the sibling temporary path in the destination directory, the write can follow a symlink and truncate a different file writable by DeckCraft. This is conditional on directory access; it is not a claim of arbitrary remote file write.

## Recommended remediation
Create a unique sibling with exclusive creation, write through its handle, then atomically replace the destination. Define and implement durability guarantees before marking the document saved or discarding recovery.

## Suggested regression coverage
In disposable directories, concurrent saves must leave one complete version, never mixed/truncated bytes. An existing temporary file/symlink must not be followed or overwritten. Cover write/rename failure without losing the prior destination.

title: [Audit] Native-format load silently ignores missing or corrupt embedded media
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/format/src/lib.rs:108-114](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/format/src/lib.rs#L108-L114) uses `if let Ok(data) = read_entry(...)` for each embedded media item and returns success after any read failure. `read_entry` reports missing members, oversized entries and read/CRC errors ([crates/format/src/lib.rs:89-96](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/format/src/lib.rs#L89-L96)), but these errors are discarded.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Open a native file whose media metadata references a missing/corrupt member, then save it. Media stays at its deserialized empty state, and the successful load gives no warning that the next save will persist lost content.

## Recommended remediation
Reject damaged required embedded media, or expose an explicit partial-recovery result with actionable warnings and protection against accidental overwrite. Treat deliberately linked media separately.

## Suggested regression coverage
Owned native-format fixtures with missing, bad-CRC and rejected-size media must produce explicit damage/recovery reporting. A normal load/save round-trip must never silently replace the original embedded content with empty data.

title: [Audit] Native ZIP import lacks an aggregate inflated-media budget
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High (availability)
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/format/src/lib.rs:20](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/format/src/lib.rs#L20) permits 2 GiB per member. The read helper at lines 89-96 has no cumulative accounting, and the media loop at lines 108-111 independently inflates every metadata entry into a retained Arc. Repeated metadata IDs can repeatedly inflate the same member into separate allocations.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Many individually accepted media entries, or duplicate references to a large member, can exhaust memory while opening a compact archive. The per-entry guard does not bound total decoded presentation memory. No allocation-exhaustion test was attempted.

## Recommended remediation
Apply cumulative inflated-byte and media-count budgets, validate media ID uniqueness, and avoid repeated inflation/retention of the same archive member. Use checked/fallible allocation where appropriate.

## Suggested regression coverage
With small test budgets, cover aggregate limit crossings, repeated member references, and exact-limit valid files. Reject before large allocations rather than constructing multi-gigabyte fixtures.

title: [Audit] AV1 tile-group parsing accepts duplicate coverage and accumulates duplicate tile state
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High (availability)

Track expected coverage/order, reject duplicate/missing/out-of-order tile groups as required by AV1, and enforce a pending payload/state budget.

At small dimensions, test valid partitioned groups plus duplicate, skipped and reordered coverage. Rejection must occur before unbounded accumulation or per-duplicate state creation.

author: PierrunoYT
body:

title: [Audit] Bitstream APIs have unchecked NAL endpoints and signed Exp-Golomb boundary errors
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High for 32-bit NAL parsing; Low for signed boundary handling
**Confidence:** High
**Verification:** Source and control-flow inspection only. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no application reproduction, exploit, or destructive/resource-exhaustion test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
1. [crates/bitstream/src/lib.rs:314-330](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/bitstream/src/lib.rs#L314-L330) checks and slices using unchecked `i + len`. With a four-byte length prefix on a 32-bit/WASM target, the endpoint can overflow. `length_size == 0` also makes no cursor progress through nonempty input (direct API case).
2. `read_se` at lines 143-146 casts positive 2147483648 into i32 when the unsigned code is at its maximum. `write_se` at lines 218-220 overflows its u32 multiplication for i32::MIN.

The NAL helper is used by both H.264 and HEVC decoders.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A malformed declared length can cause arithmetic/slice panic on 32-bit targets. Unsupported prefix width zero can loop and grow output through the public API. Extreme signed values can decode with the wrong sign or panic/wrap when encoded. These are safe-Rust correctness/availability failures, not established memory corruption.

## Recommended remediation
Validate prefix widths and forward progress, use checked endpoints, and explicitly reject signed values outside the representation or widen that representation. Prefer error-returning APIs for invalid inputs.

## Suggested regression coverage
Native and WASM/32-bit tests for truncated/oversized lengths and unsupported widths; signed extrema and neighbors must round-trip or return documented errors in both debug/release configurations.

title: [Audit] Audio playback eagerly decodes whole files with no PCM budget or cancellation
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Read-only source audit of upstream `main` at [525ec7b1a976](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/commit/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229).

**Severity:** High (availability)

[crates/media/src/audio.rs:94-109](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/525ec7b1a9769c0f73fac66ca564027c3f436229/crates/media/src/audio.rs#L94-L109),125-134,204-210 accumulates all decoded PCM in a Vec. Stream PCM through bounded buffers, impose cache-byte and concurrent-job budgets, and support cancellation when decoding is no longer needed.

## Suggested regression coverage
Use a small budget and synthetic bounded sources to test long-stream handling, cancellation after stop/close, and repeated/concurrent starts. Verify actual retained bytes and work bounds rather than only successful return.

title: Web build: run engine commands from the embedding page (a postMessage version of the control protocol)
author: MeetMellwyn
body:
**What**
Let a page that embeds the DeckCraft web build send it the engine commands the desktop app accepts on its control port (`engine.execute`, `engine.commands`, `document.inspect`), and get the results back, over `postMessage`.

**Why**
We embed the web build in a desktop app (Saxon Orc), so people can edit documents there while AI agents change the same documents with `deckcraft-cli`. Today the agent edits the file, and the open editor has to re-open it after every step. The view jumps, the undo history starts over, and the person has to stop typing while it happens. If the page could pass commands to the running editor, an agent's edits would land in the open document live, with undo, and both could work on it at once.

**Proposal**
It could follow GridCraft's `?host=parent` bridge (`apps/gridcraft-web/src/host.rs`). That bridge's `open` / `save` / `dirty` messages would be welcome here too.
- `deckcraft:execute` `{ id, command, params }` → `deckcraft:result` `{ id, ok, result | error }`: runs on the active document like `engine.execute` on the control port (one undo step per command, as on the desktop).
- `deckcraft:inspect` `{ id, text? }` → `deckcraft:result` with the `document.inspect` result.
- Only in host mode, and only from the same-origin parent window (as `host.rs` already checks), so other pages can't drive it.

We're happy to test it. Thanks for the editors!

title: CLI convert: .odp, .gif, .svg and .outline outputs silently get native .deckcraft bytes (exit 0)
author: Tokarzewski
body:
**Version:** deckcraft-cli 0.6.1, Windows x64 (the launcher's current build).

`deckcraft-cli convert IN OUT` picks the output format from OUT's extension. For `.odp`, `.gif`, `.svg` and `.outline` it exits 0, prints the output path and writes the **native `.deckcraft` bytes** under that name. Nothing says the format is unsupported.

**Steps**

```
deckcraft-cli run --sample --export in.pptx
deckcraft-cli convert in.pptx out.odp
deckcraft-cli convert in.pptx out.gif
deckcraft-cli convert in.pptx out.svg
deckcraft-cli convert in.pptx out.outline
deckcraft-cli convert in.pptx out.deckcraft
```

**Observed**

- Every command exits 0 and prints only the output path.
- `out.odp`, `out.gif`, `out.svg`, `out.outline` and `out.deckcraft` are byte-identical: 9,537 bytes, a zip (`PK\x03\x04`), the same SHA-256 (starts `e57d7719`).
- So a `.gif` or `.svg` that is really a zip, and an `.odp` that is not OpenDocument, are produced with no warning.

**Expected**

Either the format the extension names, or a non-zero exit with a clear error such as `unsupported output format .odp (supported: pptx, deckcraft, pdf, png, jpeg, ...)`. Silent substitution is the worst case for scripts, which cannot tell the output is wrong.

**Related**

- #210 covers the same pattern for `.potx` and `.ppsx`, which come out as plain presentations (I reproduced it: the main part's content type is `presentation.main+xml` for both).
- #163 is the same family for unknown `--flags` being taken as output names.

Found while generating test files headlessly with the CLI.

The remote MCP backend can use an unrelated reply as the result of a current mutation. This is pre-existing on main `457406a7a5b62425e915926c8ccb0984e61a198c` and also remains in #453; it is not claimed as a regression introduced by that PR or a duplicate of #409's lost-reply replay bug.

### Reproduction

1. A disposable loopback peer receives request ID1 and returns `{"id":999,"ok":true,"result":"unrelated"}` plus newline. The exact backend returns that unrelated result.
2. Against #453, send two newline-delimited response frames together. The extra success frame with ID999 is buffered in `BufReader`. On the next `engine.execute {command:"slide.new"}`, that buffered frame is consumed as success even though the actual current response is `ok:false`.
3. A valid JSON response followed by EOF without newline is accepted as a complete successful frame.

title: Timed-out control mutations remain queued and execute when the UI resumes
author: euisuh
body:
A control request reported as `timeout` can still execute later. This is pre-existing on main `457406a7a5b62425e915926c8ccb0984e61a198c` and is retained in #471; it is not a new bounded-queue regression.

### Concrete case

The control server queues `engine.execute {command:"slide.new"}` while the UI is not draining requests. After its 60-second wait expires, the client receives `{"ok":false,"error":"timeout"}`. When the UI resumes draining, the queued mutation is still dispatched. A user retry can therefore be followed by two executions; the old command can also act on a newly active document.

### Observed reproduction

A bounded harness using #471's exact control-server source sets its existing private test `reply_timeout` to30ms and deliberately leaves the test queue undrained. It observes the timeout reply, then retrieves the still-queued mutation. Its reply sender fails because the server has dropped the receiver. Actual later dispatch is established by the unconditional UI loop below; a full presentation app was not launched and no user data was changed.

### Source

- [Main server timeout](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/457406a7a5b62425e915926c8ccb0984e61a198c/apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs#L45-L51), retained in [#471](https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/blob/8dc068e0bacab1f058c17e270a1d7909ec02ac97/apps/deckcraft/src/control_server.rs#L152-L156).

title: [Audit] 2 crash defects with evidence and fix PRs: ASF probe arithmetic, ID3v2 tag-chain recursion
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Follow-up audit of the deckcraft media/IO path at `b1ca123` (current `main`). These two defects were listed in the earlier #727 audit, which closed when #728 landed — but the defects themselves did not land, and both are still present on current `main`. Per our audit practice, each finding ships together with its fix PR (regression tests included, red/green verified locally):

## 1. ASF probe walks objects with unchecked arithmetic — fix PR: #748

`probe_asf` (`crates/media/src/probe.rs:188`) walks ASF header objects with unchecked arithmetic: the loop guard is `while pos + 24 <= header_end` (`probe.rs:202`) and the advance is `pos += size` (`probe.rs:233`), where `size` is an uncapped 64-bit value read at `probe.rs:204`. A 64-byte file consisting of the ASF header GUID followed by 48 × `0xFF` makes `size = usize::MAX`, so the walk panics — `attempt to add with overflow` in overflow-checked builds, a slice-index panic after the wrap otherwise — and no such file can ever be probed.

Reachability: `probe()` (`probe.rs:50`) dispatches every ASF-labelled file to `probe_asf` (`probe.rs:55`), and the editor probes media on the UI thread (`ui-egui/src/media.rs:130`) whenever a file is inserted or played, outside any panic guard. The fix checks both additions so an object that overruns the header ends the walk (the correct ASF semantics), covered by the regression test `hostile_asf_object_sizes_end_the_walk`.

## 2. Chained ID3v2 tags recurse `Container::sniff` until the stack aborts — fix PR: #749

`Container::sniff` (`crates/media/src/lib.rs:76`) recurses once per ID3v2 tag: its `at(0, b"ID3")` arm (`lib.rs:94-99`) computes the tag size and calls `Container::sniff(b.get(10 + size..)…)` on line 97, so a file of N copies of a 10-byte empty ID3v2 header costs N stack frames — ~1 MB of crafted input is ~100k frames, past the main and worker stacks. The result is an uncatchable stack-overflow abort (SIGABRT), not an error: `Session::execute`'s `catch_unwind` guard cannot help,…

title: Browse for Themes applies only the theme, not the template's slide master and layouts
author: Faabyy
body:
## Problem

There's no way to apply a slide master (a company template, say) to a presentation that already exists.

In PowerPoint this is **Design › Themes › Browse for Themes…**: picking a `.potx`, `.pptx` or `.thmx` brings in that file's **slide master and its layouts** (background, master graphics such as a logo, placeholder positions, title and body text styles, footers) along with the theme. Existing slides are then mapped onto the new layouts by layout type, so their content takes the new look.

DeckCraft's Browse for Themes… (`design.browseTheme`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/design.rs`) only replaces the **theme part** of the current master (`m.theme = theme`): colours, fonts and effects. The master's shapes, backgrounds, text styles and layouts stay as they were, so a corporate template can't be applied to an existing deck.

The other ways around it don't help either:

- **Reuse Slides (Keep Source Formatting)** brings the source master, but only together with the source's slides. You can't move your own slides onto it.
- **Slide Master view** has `master.insertLayout`, `deleteLayout`, `renameLayout`, `insertPlaceholder`, `preserve` and `placeholders`, but no way to insert a master from another file.

- `docs/parity-checklist.md:105`: "Browse themes from .pptx/.thmx" is marked **D** (done).

title: macOS: .pptx / .deckcraft files cannot be opened from Finder (double-click, Open With, drop on Dock icon) — only drag-into-window works
author: infinixmedia2026
body:
Environment
DeckCraft 0.7.0 (build commit d78e657e4cb1e490ceb5445785c052d9cf5ad963), installed via ArtCraft Launcher
macOS 26.7.1 (25G241)
Apple M1 Pro, arm64
App signature: Developer ID, notarized (Gatekeeper: accepted)
Steps to reproduce
In Finder, double-click a .pptx file, or right-click → Open With, or drop the file on the DeckCraft Dock icon.
Same with a .deckcraft file saved by DeckCraft itself.
Expected
DeckCraft opens the presentation.

Actual
The file does not open in DeckCraft.

Dragging the same file into an open DeckCraft window works correctly, so the file itself is fine.

Likely cause (from inspecting the 0.7.0 bundle)
Info.plist has no CFBundleDocumentTypes. It declares UTExportedTypeDeclarations (ai.storyteller.deckcraft.presentation, .deckcraft) and UTImportedTypeDeclarations (org.openxmlformats.presentationml.presentation, .pptx), but never claims a role (Editor/Viewer) for them. So Launch Services does not register DeckCraft as an app that can open these types.
No open-document handler at runtime. The binary is built on winit 0.30.13 / eframe 0.36.2, and contains no application:openURLs: / application:openFiles: implementation on the app delegate. winit 0.30 does not forward macOS open-document events (kAEOpenDocuments) to the app, so even if the plist is fixed, the file path will not reach DeckCraft.
Drag-into-window works because it goes through winit's WindowEvent::DroppedFile, which is a separate path.
Suggested fix
Add CFBundleDocumentTypes entries for ai.storyteller.deckcraft.presentation (Owner, Editor) and org.openxmlformats.presentationml.presentation (Alternate, Editor) with LSItemContentTypes.
Implement application:openURLs: on the NSApplication delegate (e.g. via objc2-app-kit, adding the method to winit's delegate class, or a crate that handles it) and route the paths to the same code that handles DroppedFile. This must also handle files that arrive at launch, before the first window exists.

title: PPTX chart numeric data labels are ignored at series level
author: euisuh
body:
User report: numbers visible on a PowerPoint graph disappear after importing the presentation into DeckCraft. The original user presentation has not been supplied, so this issue describes independently identified source paths and synthetic reproduction coverage rather than claiming to reproduce that exact file.

At DeckCraft `1b64de3`:

- The PPTX reader stores series-level `c:dLbls/c:showVal` in `Series.data_labels`.
- Pie and bar drawing checks chart-wide `Chart.data_labels` instead of the series override. A series that requests labels can therefore render none; an explicitly hidden series can inherit unwanted labels.
- The line/area/scatter/bubble drawing path does not draw numerical data labels.
- A present `<c:showVal/>` has an optional `val` attribute whose default is true; the reader currently treats the missing attribute as unset.

Expected: import group/series visibility without leaking one combo group's settings into another, honour explicit `false`, and render enabled numerical labels for the supported chart paths.

Regression work uses contributor-generated XML/decks and checks the imported model plus actual rendered pixel differences. No proprietary PowerPoint assets or files are added.

Reference for the optional boolean default: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.drawing.charts.showvalue?view=openxml-3.0.1 . This is distinct from resolved rounding issue https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/324 .

Prepared with Codex. Platform-specific comparison against the reporter's original file remains unverified.

title: Bold CJK text drawn in regular weight: East Asian font fallback ignores the run's bold/italic
author: ibakard
body:
**DeckCraft:** 0.7.0 AppImage (`deckcraft-0.7.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage`); the code below is unchanged on `main`
**OS:** Fedora 44, x86_64 (CJK fonts: `google-noto-sans-cjk-vf-fonts`, `google-noto-serif-cjk-vf-fonts`)

## Summary

Bold Chinese, Japanese and Korean text is drawn in regular weight when the run's font has no CJK glyphs, which is the usual case: a text box in Calibri, Aptos or Arial with CJK text. Latin, Cyrillic, Hebrew and Thai text in the same paragraph is bold as expected. The same document in WordCraft 0.7.0 on the same machine draws the CJK text bold.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
# pip install python-pptx
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
prs = Presentation()
s = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
tf = s.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5), Inches(9), Inches(3)).text_frame
for text in ["你好世界 价格", "日本語 ひらがな", "한국어 안녕하세요", "Обща цена", "สวัสดีครับ"]:
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    for bold in (False, True):
        r = p.add_run(); r.text = text + "  "; r.font.name = "Calibri"; r.font.size = Pt(20); r.font.bold = bold
prs.save("cjk-bold.pptx")
```

```sh
deckcraft-cli render cjk-bold.pptx --slide 0 out.png
```

The editing canvas shows the same result, since it draws with `deckcraft_render::render_layout`.

**Expected:** the second copy of each line is bold.
**Actual:** Cyrillic and Thai are bold, but the Chinese, Japanese and Korean copies look the same as the regular ones.

## Cause

`FontDb::cascade` (`crates/fonts/src/fallback.rs`) passes the run's `style` only to the per-script path:

- Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Devanagari have `os_families` entries, so they get `self.face(fam, style)` and the bold face is used.
- CJK scripts have no entry, so they fall through to `self.fallback_for(key, exclude)`, which takes no style. `loaded_fallback_filtered` (`crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs`) sorts candidates by `(f.italic, (f.weight - 400.0).abs())`, so the regular face always wins, even when a bold face of the s…

title: deckcraft-cli audit: report hidden information in .pptx before sharing
author: ejbarraza
body:
Slide decks routinely carry information the sender doesn't know is there: speaker notes (talking points travel with the file), hidden slides, cropped images that still contain the full uncropped pixels, comments, author names, creator / last-modified-by in core properties, embedded media metadata, OLE embeddings. Cropping a photo in a slide editor doesn't delete the cropped-out region — anyone with the file can recover it.

Proposal: `deckcraft-cli audit <file>` scans the raw OPC package, reports findings as machine-readable JSON with stable finding IDs, and exits nonzero when findings exist (CI-gate usable). v1 finding classes: speaker notes, hidden slides, cropped images retaining full pixel data, comments, author PII (core/app properties), embedded media metadata, OLE embeddings.

Out of scope for v1: sanitizing (strip flagged content with a before/after report; cropped images flagged, not auto-stripped, since that's destructive) — follow-up.

Fixtures will be synthetic, built from ECMA-376 (no PowerPoint-produced files committed, per the clean-room rule).

title: Add musl Linux builds (Alpine Linux, Void musl)
author: vinod2807
body:
### What I'd like

A musl-linked Linux build, so DeckCraft runs on musl distributions — **Alpine Linux** (the most widely used musl distro, and the base of a great many container images) and **Void Linux's musl variant**. None of the currently published Linux artifacts can be used on either.

(The runtime packages a user needs *after* installing such a build are tracked separately in https://github.com/storytold/deckcraft/issues/955.)

### Why the current artifacts don't work there

The Linux tarball does contain both binaries:

```
$ tar tzf deckcraft-0.8.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz | grep /bin/
deckcraft-0.8.0-linux-x86_64/bin/deckcraft
deckcraft-0.8.0-linux-x86_64/bin/deckcraft-cli
```

…but both are linked against glibc:

```
$ file .../bin/deckcraft
  ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked,
  interpreter /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, for GNU/Linux 3.2.0, stripped

$ readelf -d .../bin/deckcraft | grep NEEDED
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libasound.so.2]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libgcc_s.so.1]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libm.so.6]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libc.so.6]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [ld-linux-x86-64.so.2]

$ .../bin/deckcraft --version
/bin/ash: .../bin/deckcraft: not found        # Alpine 3.24, i.e. musl
```

`/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` is glibc's loader; a musl system provides `/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1` instead, so the kernel cannot start the process, and the shell reports that as the very confusing "not found" — which reads like a missing file rather than an ABI mismatch. The same applies to the `.deb`, the `.rpm`, the AppImage (glibc + FUSE) and the Flatpak. `gcompat` is only a partial shim, not a real answer for a GUI application.

### The trap worth avoiding: a static musl build cannot open a window

This is the part that costs a build cycle, so it is worth writing down.

Rust's `*-unknown-linux-musl` targets **link statically by default**. A naive musl build compiles, and `deckcraft-cli` works, but the GUI ne…

title: Document the Linux runtime packages needed after a musl/Alpine install
author: vinod2807
body:
Split out of #954 in response to triage, which asked for these to be tracked separately. This ticket is **only the documentation side**; the build side (actually producing a musl artifact) stays in #954.

### Why this is worth writing down

A DeckCraft GUI loads its windowing and GPU dependencies with `dlopen`. In the current release those names appear in the binary as **strings with no matching `DT_NEEDED` entry**:

```
libX11.so.6      libXcursor.so.1      libvulkan.so.1      libwayland-client.so.0
```

Only `libasound.so.2` is a hard link-time dependency. The practical problem: when a `dlopen` target is missing, the app does not fail with a clear "requires libX" message, and a package manager cannot know about it either. It fails only at startup, so the user has no way to tell what to install. That is exactly the class of thing install instructions exist for.

### What the instructions should cover

For Alpine Linux — and Void's musl variant, which uses the same `/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1` loader:

```sh
apk add libxkbcommon libx11 libxcursor libxrandr libxi \
        wayland-libs-client \
        alsa-lib \
        vulkan-loader mesa-vulkan-swrast \
        fontconfig freetype ttf-dejavu
```

Optional, depending on what the user needs:

```sh
apk add mesa-gl mesa-egl mesa-dri-gallium   # OpenGL fallback if Vulkan is unavailable
apk add cups-client cups-libs               # printing
apk add xdg-desktop-portal                  # native file dialogs
```

Points worth spelling out:

- `alsa-lib` is DeckCraft-specific rather than generic: `deckcraft` has a hard `DT_NEEDED` on `libasound.so.2` because presentations play audio and video. The CLI does not need it.
- `mesa-vulkan-swrast` is the software Vulkan driver and works on any machine, including VMs. Users with a real GPU should install their vendor driver instead (`mesa-vulkan-intel`, `mesa-vulkan-ati`, `mesa-vulkan-nouveau`, ...).
- On older integrated GPUs with no Vulkan support the app falls back to CPU renderi…

title: Web build: let the host page supply fonts through a manifest, like PhotoCraft does
author: Tof33
body:
### Summary

On the web build, DeckCraft can only use the faces compiled into the wasm. There is no way for the page that hosts it to offer additional fonts, so a deck that relies on a brand or corporate typeface is drawn with a substitute, and a `.pptx` opened in the browser loses its intended look.

PhotoCraft already solves exactly this, and the mechanism is small. This issue asks for the same thing in DeckCraft.

### Why it matters more here than elsewhere

A presentation is a document people hand to someone else. The typeface is part of what makes it look right, and a substitution is visible on every slide — more so than in an image editor, where a missing face usually affects one text layer.

Organisations that host the web build generally have one or two mandated typefaces. Today the only way to get them in is to rebuild DeckCraft, which means leaving the published release behind and redoing the work at every version.

### What the code says

`crates/ui-egui/src/uifonts.rs`, still the case at `v0.8.0`:

> Nothing is bundled for it: on the web, where there are no installed fonts, only the embedded faces are used.

That is about script fallback, but it is the same constraint: the web build has no font source other than itself.

I checked the wasm we serve (`deckcraft-web-3d451cd28e31e9b6_bg.wasm`, ~25 MB uncompressed): `Inter` appears 94 times, while the two typefaces I would want to add appear zero times. Nothing to toggle — the faces simply are not there.

### What PhotoCraft does

PhotoCraft reads a `fonts/manifest.txt` next to the page, documented in its `HOSTING.md` under *Fonts*. One line per face:

```
Family | Style | path/to/file.otf
```

Only the first three fields are read; the path is relative to the page. Two details worth keeping if this is ported:

- the family must be the one the font **declares** (`name` table, id 16 when present, else id 1) rather than the name one would like to see in the menu — PhotoCraft warns in the console and keeps its o…

title: 0.8.0 web build panics at startup: "no pids on this platform"
author: Tof33
body:
### Summary

The `deckcraft-web-0.8.0.zip` package panics while starting up and never
shows the app. `v0.7.0`, served the same way from the same host, starts
normally — so this is a regression in 0.8.0.

### What happens

Console, in order:

```
[info]  deckcraft-web 0.8.0: wgpu backend BrowserWebGpu
[error] panicked at library/std/src/sys/process/unsupported.rs:335:5:
        no pids on this platform
[error] Uncaught RuntimeError: unreachable
```

The wasm loads fine (10.4 MB transferred, 85 ms) and the build identifies
itself, so this is not a packaging or transport problem — something on the
startup path calls into `std::process` (a pid lookup), which is `unsupported`
on `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and panics.

### Side-by-side, same host, same page

| | 0.7.0 | 0.8.0 |
|---|---|---|
| wasm loaded | yes | yes |
| version line in console | `deckcraft-web 0.7.0` | `deckcraft-web 0.8.0` |
| `event handlers installed.` | yes | never reached |
| `<canvas>` size | 2108×1622 | 300×150 (untouched default) |
| panic | — | `no pids on this platform` |

The canvas size is the clearest tell: 300×150 is the HTML default, so the app
never got as far as sizing its own surface.

### Reproduction

1. Serve `deckcraft-web-0.8.0/` as a static directory (any host; I use a
   plain static file server, wasm served with `application/wasm`).
2. Open `index.html`.
3. The page stays blank; the console shows the panic above.

Chromium 141, macOS 15.5, WebGPU available (0.7.0 uses it on the same
machine).

### Note

`guard.rs:29` logs the panic as `ERROR: [deckcraft_engine::guard] panic at …`
just before it propagates, so the guard sees it — that may be a good place to
start looking for who asks for a pid.

Happy to test a build.
